interactions.purpose: Build a reusable Agent Skill that records the AI audit trail required by HW04
interactions.prompt: [EXCERPT - full brief in the session transcript] I am working on HW04 - Automation Testing. The assignment requires the entire AI-use process to be recorded in a complete log (AI tool name, date/time, prompt, AI output) and encourages building Agent Skills that perform these activities automatically. Create a production-quality Agent Skill named `ai-audit-logger` that can: start an audit session; record an AI interaction; classify AI usage; explicitly capture HUMAN REVIEW as distinct from AI OUTPUT and HUMAN ACTION; track AI mistakes and missed items with severity/cause/correction/resolution; maintain ai-audit-log.json as the machine-readable source of truth and generate AI_Audit_Report.md from it; validate audit completeness with PASS/WARNING/ERROR; never store secrets; never invent missing information; stay reusable across features (FR-01 Registration, FR-08 Checkout), AI tools and future assignments. Provide the complete skill: directory structure, SKILL.md, supporting templates, example log, example report, workflow, install and validation instructions, and a demonstration scenario (fragile CSS selector found and corrected).
interactions.ai_output: [Files, not chat text] Produced .claude/skills/ai-audit-logger/ containing: SKILL.md (frontmatter + workflow + rules); scripts/audit.py (470 lines, Python stdlib only; subcommands init/log/update/issue/list/validate/report/selftest, JSON on stdin, auto IDs A001.., auto timestamps, credential redaction, built-in selftest); reference/fields.md (field dictionary, open category list, issue types); examples/ (README.md demo walkthrough + generated ai-audit-log.json and AI_Audit_Report.md for the FR-01 fragile-selector scenario). Verified by running `audit.py selftest` -> selftest OK, and by generating the example report (3 interactions, 4 issues, validate = 2 pass / 1 warning / 0 error).
interactions.human_review: Structure and behaviour accepted. Two gaps surfaced while actually using it: (1) the skill shipped with no way visible to me to put my own name and student ID in - I had to ask; (2) the documentation used a bare `A` as the shell shorthand, which collides visually with the interaction IDs A001/A002 and left me unsure whether `A` was part of the tool. I also did not initially understand whether the skill is run in a separate terminal or inside Claude Code.
interactions.human_action: Accepted the skill. Ran `audit init` with my real name (Nguyen Tran Minh Tuan) and MSSV 20127420 to create the project audit log. Requested a plain usage document, which became docs/AI_Audit_Logger_HOWTO.md. Requested the shorthand be renamed from `A` to `audit`.
interactions.reason_for_modification: Usability of the documentation, not correctness of the tool.

issues.description: argparse: --path and --no-redact were defined on the parent parser, so `audit.py log --path X` was rejected
issues.why: Known argparse behaviour - a parent-level option placed after a subcommand is not parsed. The AI wrote the common options once at the top without accounting for it.
issues.human_correction: Caught by the AI's own built-in selftest on first run (not by human review); fixed by moving both options into a shared parent parser passed to every subparser.
issues.resolution: Fixed before delivery. selftest OK. Options now go after the subcommand.

interactions.purpose: Build a reusable Agent Skill that turns HW04 test cases into data-driven Playwright scripts (CSV data, >=3 assertions, 3 browsers, HTML report stamped with student name/ID)
interactions.prompt:
Create an Agent Skill named `automation-test-builder` for my HW04 Automation Testing assignment.

Its purpose is to convert test cases into maintainable Playwright automation scripts following these fixed requirements:

1. Data-driven testing - Test data MUST be stored in a separate .csv file. Do NOT use hardcoded inline arrays or objects for test data. Playwright tests must load and use the CSV data. The Skill should support multiple test cases and datasets.
2. Assertions - Generated tests must use at least 3 distinct assertion patterns, for example: toHaveURL(), toHaveText()/toContainText(), toBeVisible()/toBeHidden(), toHaveValue(), toBeEnabled()/toBeDisabled(). Choose assertions that are appropriate to the actual test scenario rather than adding meaningless assertions just to satisfy the count.
3. Browsers - Configure Playwright to run every feature on Chrome, Edge, Firefox. Each feature must be executable on all 3 browsers.
4. HTML reports - Use Playwright HTML Reporter. Every test run must produce an HTML report that visibly contains: `Run by: 20127420 - Nguyễn Trần Minh Tuấn`. Prefer configuring this through Playwright reporter/project metadata rather than manually modifying the generated report after execution.
5. Input - The Skill should accept: Feature/requirement, Test cases, Test data requirements, SUT information, Existing selectors or page information when available. It should generate: Playwright .spec.js or .spec.ts, Separate .csv test-data file, Playwright configuration for Chrome, Edge and Firefox, HTML reporter configuration.
6. Quality rules - Generated scripts should: prefer stable semantic locators (getByRole, getByLabel, etc.); avoid unnecessary hard waits such as waitForTimeout(); include meaningful assertions; avoid duplicated test logic; be reusable and maintainable; never invent selectors, URLs, or application behavior when the provided information does not support them, clearly mark missing information instead.
7. Workflow - Test Cases -> Analyze test steps/data -> Design CSV test data -> Generate data-driven Playwright tests -> Apply >=3 assertion patterns -> Configure Chrome/Edge/Firefox -> Configure HTML Reporter with `Run by: 20127420` -> Validate the generated files -> Provide a short summary of assumptions and potential issues.
8. Deliverables - Create the complete Agent Skill, including: SKILL.md, recommended folder structure, any necessary templates/config files, one small example using a fictional login feature, concise usage instructions.

Design it so I can reuse the same Skill for FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, etc. without modifying the Skill itself. Before presenting the final Skill, verify that it satisfies every requirement above.
interactions.ai_output:
[Files, not chat text] Created .claude/skills/automation-test-builder/ with 11 files:

- SKILL.md - frontmatter (name + trigger description), Usage block, Input contract table (what to ask for, what to emit as TODO_ when absent), Output layout, 8-step workflow (analyse -> design CSV -> generate spec -> >=3 assertions -> 3 browsers -> HTML report title -> validate -> summarise assumptions), Quality rules (locator priority, no waitForTimeout, single flow per feature, tc_id in test titles), Files list.
- templates/playwright.config.ts - projects chrome (channel 'chrome'), edge (channel 'msedge'), firefox; reporter [['html', { outputFolder: 'playwright-report', open: 'never', title: `Run by: ${RUN_BY}` }], ['list']]; baseURL from process.env.BASE_URL with TODO_BASE_URL fallback.
- templates/fixtures.ts - zero-dependency RFC4180-ish CSV parser (quoted fields, embedded commas/newlines, "" escapes, CRLF, BOM), readCsv() resolved from process.cwd(), isTrue() helper, and `test` extended with an auto fixture pushing annotation { type: 'Run by', description: '20127420 - Nguyen Tran Minh Tuan' } onto every test.
- templates/fixtures.check.spec.ts - unit check for the CSV parser, runs without a browser.
- templates/feature.spec.ts + templates/feature.csv - per-feature skeletons; spec reads the CSV at module level and loops `for (const row of rows) test(...)`, branching on isTrue(row.expect_success).
- examples/login/ - fictional FR-00 login: login.spec.ts, login.csv (4 datasets), README.md, and a 2-page static demo app (login.html + dashboard.html) so the example runs offline.

Verification actually executed in a scratchpad copy of the project (demo app served on localhost):
- `npx playwright test --list` -> 12 tests (4 CSV rows x 3 browser projects); proves data comes from the CSV.
- `npx playwright test --project=chrome --project=edge` -> 10 passed.
- CSV parser unit check passed on all 3 projects.
- Rendered the generated HTML report with Playwright and read the DOM: .header-title = "Run by: 20127420 - Nguyen Tran Minh Tuan"; each test detail page shows the same string as a "Run by" annotation.
- 5 assertion patterns used in the example: toBeEnabled, toHaveValue, toHaveURL, toBeVisible, toContainText.

Not verified: Firefox execution. The bundled Playwright Firefox on this machine fails to launch with "Could not find profile folder", reproduced outside Playwright by launching the binary manually with an explicit -profile directory, and still failing after `npx playwright install --force firefox`. The firefox project is configured and enumerates correctly; only the local browser binary is broken.

issues.description: The 'Run by: 20127420 - Nguyễn Trần Minh Tuấn' stamp was first implemented with Playwright's config.metadata, which renders nothing in the HTML report of the installed version (1.63) - the Metadata panel expands empty.
issues.why: The AI followed the user's hint ('reporter/project metadata') from general knowledge of newer Playwright releases instead of checking what this project's version actually renders.
issues.resolution: Caught by the AI's own verification (rendered the generated report in a browser and read the DOM) before delivery. Replaced with the html reporter's `title` option, re-run and confirmed as .header-title in the report; the per-test 'Run by' annotation from fixtures.ts was kept as a second, independently verified location. SKILL.md now warns against config.metadata.

issues.description: SKILL.md's validation step told the user to verify the report stamp with `grep -r "20127420" playwright-report/index.html`, which always returns 0 matches.
issues.why: The AI assumed the HTML report embeds its data as plain text; in this version the report payload is compressed, so the string is not greppable.
issues.resolution: Found while running the step; replaced with `npx playwright show-report` plus an explicit note that the stamp lives in the compressed payload and must be checked in the rendered report.

issues.description: SKILL.md's validation step included `npx tsc --noEmit ...` although TypeScript is not a dependency of this project; running it made npx install an unrelated deprecated package (tsc@2.0.4) instead of type-checking.
issues.why: The AI added a conventional type-check step without checking the project's devDependencies (only @playwright/test and @types/node).
issues.resolution: Removed the step. Playwright transpiles the specs itself and `npx playwright test --list` already catches load-time errors.

issues.description: The CSV-parser self-check was first written as a standalone Node script (.ts, then .mts) that failed twice - 'Cannot use import statement outside a module', then 'does not provide an export named isTrue' - because the project is CommonJS while fixtures.ts uses ESM syntax.
issues.why: The AI relied on Node 24 TypeScript type-stripping without accounting for the package's commonjs module type and the ESM/CJS named-export lexing limits.
issues.resolution: Abandoned the standalone runner; the check ships as templates/fixtures.check.spec.ts, run by Playwright's own transpiler - verified passing on all 3 browser projects.

interactions.purpose: Measure the real lockout behaviour of the SUT and classify every failing assertion as a genuine defect or a test defect.
interactions.prompt:
Please help me create Playwright test cases for automation testing. The system specifications are described in @"docs/System Requirements Specification.md", I have the system running and ready. I want to start with test cases for the FR-02 function, test cases I think are manually described in @docs/HW04.md, The limit is 12 test cases per function; please let me know if any seem redundant, lack context, or are untestable, and feel free to suggest any additional test cases you think should be included.

interactions.ai_output:
Measured against freshly registered accounts, then confirmed in the SUT source.

Execution: 24 runs on Chrome + Edge, 14 passed, 10 failed. All 10 failures are genuine product defects, identical on both browsers.

1. Account locks after 2 consecutive failures, FR-02 requires 3.
   backend/server.js:54  const newAttempts = user.login_attempts + 2;   (should be + 1)
2. Lockout lasts 180 seconds, FR-02 specifies 30.
   backend/server.js:57  new Date(Date.now() + 180000)                  (should be 30000)
3. Email field is not type=email, so HTML5 format validation never runs.
   frontend-web/src/pages/Login.jsx:30
4. Password field renders its value in clear text.
   frontend-web/src/pages/Login.jsx:40
5. CRITICAL - the login response returns the account's password to the client.
   backend/server.js:52  res.json({ message, token, user })  serialises the whole row.

Passing cases confirm real behaviour too: FR02-TC10 shows an unknown email and a wrong password return byte-identical responses, so there is no user enumeration.
interactions.human_review: Not recorded as an independent verification. The user accepted the defect list by asking for it to be written into docs/Report.md section 6. The source line citations were re-checked against the SUT before writing.
interactions.human_action: Directed the 5 defects into docs/Report.md section 6. GitHub Issues not yet filed.

issues.description: Reported the wrong lockout threshold. The first probe ran against the shared test@eshop.com account and concluded that the account locks after 2 consecutive failures. That reading was an artefact of contaminated state, not the product's behaviour.
issues.why: The account already carried a failed attempt from an earlier UI interaction in the same session, so login_attempts did not start at 0. The AI measured a stateful counter without first establishing a clean starting state, and reported the observation as a finding without questioning where the state had come from.
issues.human_correction: Re-measured on a freshly registered account via POST /api/register, which showed the threshold is crossed on the 3rd attempt. The true defect (the counter increments by 2 instead of 1) was then confirmed by reading backend/server.js:54.
issues.resolution: Fixed. The suite now registers a private account per test row so every measurement starts from login_attempts = 0. The published defect list reflects the corrected reading.

interactions.purpose: Get a third browser running for the multi-browser requirement after Firefox failed to launch.
interactions.prompt:
[user, after being offered the choice to swap to WebKit or try to fix Firefox] Try to fix Firefox

[later] I've tried reloading Firefox - please check if it's working now. If it still doesn't work, try using the Zen browser (which I've already installed on the machine).

[later] What bout floorp, can it work?

[later] I just installed floorp, please check again.
interactions.ai_output:
Firefox is blocked by a host-environment fault, not by the test code. Two distinct failures on macOS 26 / Darwin 27, Apple Silicon:
  firefox-1543 (FF 155, Playwright 1.63) -> 'Could not find profile folder' in headless
  firefox-1490 (FF 141, Playwright 1.55) -> launches, then deadlocks with
     'RenderCompositorSWGL failed mapping default framebuffer'

Attempted and ruled out: reinstall; --force reinstall; disabling the sandbox; headed mode; re-signing the app bundle inside-out after finding its code signature invalid (Sealed Resources=none, which caused macOS to SIGKILL Firefox's child processes); pinning Playwright 1.55; disabling WebRender and the GPU process via prefs and env vars.

Firefox forks are NOT a substitute. Playwright drives Firefox over the Juggler protocol, which exists only in Playwright's patched builds:
  unzip -l Zen.app/Contents/Resources/omni.ja    | grep -ci juggler  -> 0
  unzip -l Floorp.app/Contents/Resources/omni.ja | grep -ci juggler  -> 0
  unzip -l <playwright firefox>/omni.ja          | grep -ci juggler  -> 19
Floorp was additionally confirmed by a real launch attempt, which failed. Playwright 1.63 exposes no public WebDriver BiDi browser type (only chromium/firefox/webkit), so no stock Firefox build can be driven.

WebKit was verified working on this machine and is available as a substitute. Docker is installed but the daemon was not running; the official mcr.microsoft.com/playwright Linux image has neither fault.
interactions.human_review: The user rejected the AI's first recommendation (swap Firefox for WebKit) and directed it to fix Firefox instead, then proposed Zen and Floorp as alternatives. Both proposals were investigated and shown to be structurally impossible rather than merely unconfigured.
interactions.human_action: Deferred Firefox ('I'll figure out how to get Firefox working later') and redirected the session back to FR-02. The firefox project was kept in playwright.config.ts; the suite currently covers 24 of 36 runs.
interactions.reason_for_modification: No code change resolved it - the fault is in the host environment's Firefox build, outside the test suite.
